message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance as international hubs:

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Key gateway to Asia and Latin America; major hub for American Airlines and United. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD) | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the busiest airports in the U.S.; major hub for United and American. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-runway airports. |
| Denver International Airport (DEN) | Denver, CO | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; hub for United and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) | New York City, NY | JFK | Primary gateway to Europe; major hub for American and Delta. |
| San Francisco International Airport (SFO) | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Major hub for United and a key gateway to Asia. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA) | Seattle, WA | SEA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport (MIA) | Miami, FL | MIA | Major hub for American and a key gateway to Latin America. |
| Orlando International Airport (MCO) | Orlando, FL | MCO | Major hub for Southwest and a popular destination for leisure travelers. |

These airports serve as major hubs for airlines, have extensive international connections, and handle millions of passengers each year.
